explanation: Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) is 26 November, the day the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution in 1949; it has been officially observed since 2015. January 26 is Republic Day, the date the Constitution came into force in 1950 — that is the classic trap here.

Nasim Zaidi was Chief Election Commissioner from 19 April 2015 to 5 July 2017, so he held the post when this 2016 paper was set. H.S. Brahma preceded him (Jan–Apr 2015) and A.K. Jyoti succeeded him in 2017. The CEC is appointed under Article 324.

Lord Curzon announced the Partition of Bengal in July 1905 and it took effect on 16 October 1905, triggering the Swadeshi movement; it was annulled in 1911. 1906 is the year of the Muslim League's founding and the Calcutta Congress session, not the partition.

In the three-tier Panchayati Raj structure created by the 73rd Amendment (Article 243B), the Panchayat Samiti is the intermediate tier at the block/taluka level, between the Gram Panchayat (village) and the Zila Parishad (district).

Raja Ram Mohan Roy, founder of the Brahmo Samaj and campaigner against sati, is conventionally called the Father of the Indian Renaissance and of modern India. Ambedkar, Tilak and Gokhale belong to later phases of the national movement.
The Zila Parishad, at district level, is the apex body of the three-tier Panchayati Raj system, with the Panchayat Samiti (block) in the middle and Gram Panchayat (village) at the base.

Yellow Revolution denotes the sharp rise in oilseed (especially mustard and sunflower) production from the mid-1980s under the Technology Mission on Oilseeds. Eggs belong to the Silver Revolution and food grains to the Green Revolution.

Census 2011 counted cultivators (24.6%) plus agricultural labourers (30.0%) at about 54.6% of all workers, which rounds to the 55% option. The question's '2010–11 Census' label is loose — the census was 2011 — and the exact figure depends on whether marginal workers are included, so treat 55% as the intended approximation.

Fair Price Shops (ration shops) are the retail outlets of the Public Distribution System, which delivers subsidised food grain to card holders. Buffer stock operations and Minimum Support Price relate to procurement and price support, not to the retail sale itself.

India's balance-of-payments deficits have been driven simultaneously by a large import bill (crude oil and gold), sluggish export growth, and weaker invisible receipts, so all three listed causes apply.

The Coromandel coast from Visakhapatnam down to Tamil Nadu is struck mainly by post-monsoon (retreating monsoon) cyclones in October and November, when Bay of Bengal sea-surface temperatures and low-pressure formation peak. The pre-monsoon May peak affects mostly the north Bay (Odisha, Bengal, Bangladesh).

The Green Revolution was confined largely to cereals — wheat and later rice — through HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, pesticides and assured irrigation; it did not target vegetables. Vegetable and horticulture expansion is a later development, sometimes labelled the Golden/Rainbow Revolution.
In Census migration data, marriage is overwhelmingly the leading reason for female migration in India (patrilocal residence), whereas work and employment dominate male migration.
Census 2011 put female literacy at 65.46% against male literacy of 82.14% and an overall rate of 74.04%. The other options are near-miss decoys around the same figure.

The Prime Minister of India is the ex-officio President of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR); the Union Minister of Science and Technology is its Vice-President. The President of India heads no such body ex officio.

The Government of India Act 1858 ended Company rule and made the Governor-General of India also the Viceroy, i.e. the direct representative of the British Crown — Lord Canning was the first. The option is misprinted as 'Viceroy of the state' when the actual title was Viceroy of India, but it is plainly the intended answer.

Lord Mountbatten stayed on as the first Governor-General of the Dominion of India from 15 August 1947 to June 1948. C. Rajagopalachari was the second and last Governor-General, and Rajendra Prasad became the first President in 1950 — both are the usual traps.
Shaktikanta Das took charge as RBI Governor on 12 December 2018, succeeding Urjit Patel, so he was the incumbent when this 2019 paper was set.

Under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968, one route to national party status is polling at least 6% of valid votes in four or more states in a Lok Sabha or Assembly general election (with at least four Lok Sabha seats). Presence in every state or forming governments in three states is not a statutory criterion.

M1 (currency with the public + demand deposits + other deposits with RBI) is the narrow money measure and the most liquid; liquidity falls as you move to M2, M3 (broad money) and M4, which add progressively less-liquid post office and time deposits.

The jump in edible-oil output from hybrid oilseeds under the Technology Mission on Oilseeds (1986) is called the Yellow Revolution. White Revolution refers to milk (Operation Flood) and Brown Revolution to leather/cocoa or non-conventional products.

Both statements are wrong: the double-entry record of all economic transactions between residents and the rest of the world is the balance of payments, not the balance of trade (which covers only merchandise); and transactions in goods, services and income belong to the current account, not the capital account.

A loan or advance against an LIC policy is granted as a percentage (typically up to 85–90%) of its surrender value, which is why the policy must have run long enough to acquire one. Face value and paid-up value matter only indirectly, through the surrender value calculation; the question's wording 'advance value' is non-standard.

All four statements about the Government of India Act 1919 are correct: it is the Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms; dyarchy transferred certain provincial subjects to Indian ministers; the central legislature had no real control over the Governor-General and his Executive Council; and the franchise, based on property and tax qualifications, covered only a tiny fraction of the population.

M.N. Roy first proposed a Constituent Assembly for India in 1934; the Congress adopted the demand officially in 1935, and it was conceded through the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946. Rajendra Prasad later presided over the Assembly but did not originate the idea.

The Rule of Law, embodied in Article 14, is borrowed from Britain, where A.V. Dicey formulated it (supremacy of law, equality before law, predominance of legal spirit). Judicial review and due process influences come from the USA, so that option is the usual distractor.

Article 365 provides that where a state fails to comply with directions of the Union, the President may hold that a situation has arisen in which the government of the state cannot be carried on per the Constitution — the trigger for President's Rule under Article 356. The President cannot directly dismiss a state Council of Ministers or deploy force as the constitutional remedy.

Panchayati Raj Institutions, constitutionalised by the 73rd Amendment (Part IX, Articles 243–243O), transfer political authority to elected local bodies and are the standard example of political decentralisation. Political parties and pressure groups are actors within the system, not devolved units of government.

'Planning from below' means plans originating in village and block bodies rather than being imposed from the centre, which is precisely the grassroots-democracy idea behind district planning committees (Article 243ZD) and Panchayati Raj.

In the standard political-theory classification, freedom to form associations and unions is a civil right — one enjoyed by every person as a member of society — as against political rights such as voting or holding office, which attach only to citizens. In Indian constitutional terms it is a Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(c); some textbooks class it as political, so the options are arguable.
'India in Transition' (1922) was written by M.N. Roy, the founder of the Communist Party of India in exile. Dadabhai Naoroji's famous work is 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.

The Planning Commission was created by a Cabinet Resolution of the Government of India on 15 March 1950 — an extra-constitutional, non-statutory body with the Prime Minister as Chairman. It was replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015, also by executive resolution.
Rice is India's principal food crop by area sown and by consumption, grown across the eastern and southern states as well as the irrigated north-west. Wheat is second and is the dominant rabi cereal.

The 'plan holiday' covered 1966–69, when the Third Plan's failure, the 1965 war, drought and rupee devaluation forced three annual plans in place of a Five Year Plan; the Fourth Plan therefore began only in 1969.

Economic development, unlike mere growth in output, involves structural change — a shifting sectoral composition of national income — together with a corresponding shift in the occupational structure from agriculture to industry and services, so both (a) and (b) hold.

The Central Statistical Organisation (now the National Statistical Office under MoSPI) compiles and publishes the national income estimates. The NSSO conducts the sample surveys that feed into them, and the National Income Committee of 1949 (Mahalanobis, Gadgil, Rao) was a one-time body that led to the CSO's creation.

Central economic planning with state-set targets and allocation of resources is the defining institutional feature of a socialist economy, as in the Soviet model India partly borrowed from. A mixed economy such as India's adopted planning, but planning is not what defines it — the coexistence of public and private sectors is.

The Bombay Stock Exchange, tracing to 1875 as 'The Native Share and Stock Brokers' Association', is the oldest stock exchange in India and in Asia. The NSE was set up only in 1992 and began trading in 1994.

SEBI was established on 12 April 1988 by a government resolution as a non-statutory regulator; it acquired statutory status only on 30 January 1992 through the SEBI Act, 1992. Because the paper offers both years, 1988 is correct for 'established' while 1992 would be correct for 'made statutory' — a genuinely ambiguous item.
'Economic and social planning' is Entry 20 of the Concurrent List in the Seventh Schedule, which is why both the Union and the states could legislate and plan in this field.

Indira Gandhi coined 'Garibi Hatao' in the 1971 campaign, and poverty removal with self-reliance became the declared objective of the Fifth Five Year Plan (1974–79). The Fourth Plan (1969–74), whose watchwords were growth with stability, is the common distractor.
Anamudi in the Idukki district of Kerala (2,695 m) is the highest peak in South India and in the Western Ghats. Doddabetta and Makurti are lower Nilgiri peaks, and Nanda Devi is in the Himalayas.
The Kolar Gold Fields lie in Kolar district of Karnataka; once among the world's deepest mines, they were closed in 2001.
Bokaro Thermal Power Station is in Bokaro district of Jharkhand (part of the erstwhile Bihar until 2000), sited on the Damodar valley coalfields.
West Bengal has the largest concentration of jute mills in India, clustered along the Hooghly river, benefiting from raw jute from the Ganga delta, cheap water transport, and the Kolkata port.

Kerala permits the sale of alcohol through state-run and licensed outlets, whereas Gujarat, Bihar (since 2016) and Nagaland enforce prohibition. Kerala's brief 2014 partial-ban policy was rolled back, so it is the odd one out.
